claim: KNDy neurons are glutamatergic and synthesize at least four neuropeptides including kisspeptin, NKB, dynorphin, and galanin.
source: The kisspeptin neurons located in the arcuate/infundibular nucleus of the mammalian hypothalamus appear to engage in substantial co-transmission being glutamatergic and synthesizing at least four neuropeptides including kisspeptin, NKB, dynorphin, and galanin (Lehman et al., 2010; Skrapits et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Lehman et al., 2010; Skrapits et al., 2015).

claim: In a range of mammals, the majority of arcuate nucleus neurons co-express kisspeptin, NKB, and dynorphin.
source: In a range of mammals, the majority of these arcuate nucleus (ARN) neurons co-express kisspeptin, NKB, and dynorphin resulting in their 'KNDy' moniker (Lehman et al., 2010; Skrapits et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Lehman et al., 2010; Skrapits et al., 2015).

claim: The three neuropeptides (kisspeptin, NKB, and dynorphin) are packaged within separate vesicles within KNDy nerve terminals.
source: Immunohistochemical studies have demonstrated that the three neuropeptides are packaged within separate vesicles within KNDy nerve terminals (Lehman et al., 2010; Murakawa et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior immunohistochemical studies (Lehman et al., 2010; Murakawa et al., 2016).

claim: KNDy neurons project widely throughout the limbic system.
source: Although the KNDy neurons project widely throughout the limbic system (Krajewski et al., 2010; Yeo and Herbison, 2011; Yip et al., 2015), they are best characterized as being the 'GnRH pulse generator' responsible for episodically activating the gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neurons to drive pulsatile luteinizing hormone (LH) secretion (Clarkson et al., 2017; Herbison, 2018; Plant, 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Krajewski et al., 2010; Yeo and Herbison, 2011; Yip et al., 2015).

claim: KNDy neurons are the 'GnRH pulse generator' responsible for episodically activating GnRH neurons to drive pulsatile LH secretion.
source: Although the KNDy neurons project widely throughout the limbic system (Krajewski et al., 2010; Yeo and Herbison, 2011; Yip et al., 2015), they are best characterized as being the 'GnRH pulse generator' responsible for episodically activating the gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neurons to drive pulsatile luteinizing hormone (LH) secretion (Clarkson et al., 2017; Herbison, 2018; Plant, 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Clarkson et al., 2017; Herbison, 2018; Plant, 2019).

claim: KNDy neurons provide an episodic stimulatory input to the distal projections of GnRH neurons close to their secretory zone in the median eminence.
source: The KNDy neurons are proposed to achieve this by providing an episodic stimulatory input to the distal projections of the GnRH neurons close to their secretory zone in the median eminence (ME) (Herbison, 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Herbison, 2018).

claim: The distal projections of GnRH neurons have shared features of dendrites and axons and have been termed 'dendrons'.
source: These distal projections of the GnRH neuron have shared features of dendrites and axons and have been termed 'dendrons' (Herde et al., 2013; Herbison, 2016; Moore et al., 2018b; Yip et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Herde et al., 2013; Herbison, 2016; Moore et al., 2018b; Yip et al., 2021).

claim: 68.5 ± 6.2% of analyzed GnRH dendron segments had at least one apposition with a kisspeptin fiber.
source: We found that 68.5 ± 6.2% of analyzed GnRH dendrons segments had at least one apposition with a kisspeptin fiber (N = 4 female mice).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from 4 female mice.

claim: 4.0 ± 0.4 kisspeptin close appositions per 100 μm of dendron length were observed.
source: In total, we observed 4.0 ± 0.4 kisspeptin close appositions/100 μm of dendron length and 67.0 ± 7.6% of these co-expressed NKB (Figure 1A; N = 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from 4 mice and referenced in Figure 1A.

claim: 67.0 ± 7.6% of kisspeptin close appositions co-expressed NKB.
source: In total, we observed 4.0 ± 0.4 kisspeptin close appositions/100 μm of dendron length and 67.0 ± 7.6% of these co-expressed NKB (Figure 1A; N = 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from 4 mice and referenced in Figure 1A.

claim: GnRH neuron projections are innervated by KNDy neurons in addition to preoptic area kisspeptin neurons that do not express NKB.
source: Prior work has shown that the GnRH neuron projections are innervated by KNDy neurons in addition to preoptic area kisspeptin neurons that do not express NKB (Yip et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Yip et al., 2015).

claim: Each kisspeptin/NKB fiber made close appositions with 4.5 ± 0.7 GnRH neuron dendrons on average.
source: On average, each kisspeptin/NKB fiber made close appositions with 4.5 ± 0.7 GnRH neuron dendrons.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: KNDy neurons provide abundant, divergent innervation of the GnRH neuron distal dendrons.
source: This arrangement suggests an abundant, divergent innervation of the GnRH neuron distal dendrons by KNDy neurons.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the anatomical data showing multiple appositions.

claim: No kisspeptin-containing synaptic profiles were identified on 45 individual distal dendrons examined using expansion microscopy.
source: Surprisingly, we identified no kisspeptin-containing synaptic profiles on 45 individual distal dendrons (>15 µm length each, N = 3 mice) with all kisspeptin/synaptophysin-immunoreactive boutons being outside the criteria for a synapse or indeed quite separate from the GFP-expressing dendron (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by expansion microscopy data from 3 mice and referenced in Figures 1B and 1C.

claim: The average distance between kisspeptin–synaptophysin boutons and GnRH neuron dendrons was 2.22 ± 0.27 µm (post-expansion).
source: The average distance between kisspeptin–synaptophysin boutons and GnRH neuron dendrons was 2.22 ± 0.27 µm (post-expansion).
evidence: The claim is supported by expansion microscopy measurements.

claim: Many synaptophysin-expressing boutons without kisspeptin make synaptic appositions with GnRH neuron dendrons at a density of 2.3 ± 0.1 synaptophysin synapses per 10 µm dendron.
source: Nevertheless, many synaptophysin-expressing boutons without kisspeptin were identified to make synaptic appositions with GnRH neuron dendrons (density of 2.3 ± 0.1 synaptophysin synapses per 10 µm dendron) (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by expansion microscopy data and referenced in Figure 1B.

claim: 37.9 ± 0.8% of all synaptophysin boutons synapsing on GnRH neuron soma/proximal dendrites contained kisspeptin.
source: Overall, 37.9 ± 0.8% of all synaptophysin boutons synapsing on GnRH neuron soma/proximal dendrites (0.81 ± 0.44 per 10 μm) contained kisspeptin.
evidence: The claim is supported by expansion microscopy data from GnRH neuron soma/proximal dendrites.

claim: Kisspeptin inputs to the GnRH cell bodies and proximal dendrites exist as classical synapses.
source: These observations indicate that while kisspeptin inputs to the GnRH cell bodies and proximal dendrites exist as classical synapses, this is not the case for the distal dendron where divergent KNDy signaling occurs through short-diffusion volume transmission.
evidence: The claim is inferred from expansion microscopy data showing synaptic profiles at soma/proximal dendrites.

claim: Divergent KNDy signaling to the distal dendron occurs through short-diffusion volume transmission.
source: These observations indicate that while kisspeptin inputs to the GnRH cell bodies and proximal dendrites exist as classical synapses, this is not the case for the distal dendron where divergent KNDy signaling occurs through short-diffusion volume transmission.
evidence: The claim is inferred from expansion microscopy data showing no synapses at distal dendrons.

claim: KNDy neurons exhibit synchronized episodes of activity for 1–2 min prior to each LH pulse in vivo.
source: In vivo recordings show that KNDy neurons exhibit synchronized episodes of activity for 1–2 min prior to each LH pulse (Han et al., 2019; McQuillan et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior in vivo recording studies (Han et al., 2019; McQuillan et al., 2019).

claim: Application of a 90 s puff of kisspeptin (100 nM) generated a 35.1 ± 0.1% rise in dendron [Ca2+] in males and 40.5 ± 0.2% in females.
source: Application of a 90 s puff of kisspeptin (100 nM) generated a 35.1 ± 0.1% (mean ± SEM, male, median 35.1%) to 40.5 ± 0.2% (female, median 40.1%) rise in dendron [Ca2+] that peaked and then gradually subsided across the 400 s duration of the recording in both male (N = 7) and female (N = 5) mice (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by GCaMP6 imaging data from 7 male and 5 female mice and referenced in Figures 3C and 3D.

claim: Approximately 91% of dendrons responded to kisspeptin.
source: Approximately 91% of dendrons responded to kisspeptin.
evidence: The claim is supported by GCaMP6 imaging data.

claim: 90 s puffs of glutamate (600 μM) had no significant effects on dendron [Ca2+] in either males or females.
source: In contrast, 90 s puffs of glutamate (600 μM) that would activate both ionotropic and metabotropic receptors were found to have no significant effects on dendron [Ca2+] in either males (N = 9) or females (N = 2) (Figure 3E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by GCaMP6 imaging data from 9 male and 2 female mice and referenced in Figures 3E and 3F.

claim: 90 s puffs of AMPA (80 μM) had no effects on dendron [Ca2+] in males or females.
source: Furthermore, 90 s puffs of AMPA (80 μM) had no effects on dendron [Ca2+] in males (N = 5) or females (N = 2) (Figure 3G,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by GCaMP6 imaging data from 5 male and 2 female mice and referenced in Figures 3G and 3H.

claim: NMDA (200 μM) given as two 30 s puffs in the absence of Mg2+ had no effects on dendron [Ca2+] in males or females.
source: Similarly, N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA )(200 μM) given as two 30 s puffs in the absence of Mg2+ had no effects in males (N = 4) or females (N = 5) (Figure 3I–J).
evidence: The claim is supported by GCaMP6 imaging data from 4 male and 5 female mice and referenced in Figures 3I and 3J.

claim: 90 second puffs of 100 nM NKB generated small rises in dendron [Ca2+] (male, 2.45 ± 0.04%, female, 4.73 ± 0.05%) that were not significantly different to control aCSF puffs.
source: Ninety second puffs of 100 nM NKB generated small rises in dendron [Ca2+] (male, 2.45 ± 0.04% [mean ± SEM], median 2.54%; female, 4.73 ± 0.05%, median 4.64%) that were not significantly different to control aCSF puffs in either males (N = 11) or females (N = 5) (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by GCaMP6 imaging data from 11 male and 5 female mice and referenced in Figures 4A and 4B.

claim: Identical puffs of 100 nM NKB directly above KNDy neurons exerted potent stimulatory effects on [Ca2+] in both males and females.
source: To ensure that this was not a technical false negative, horizontal brain slices were prepared from Kiss1Cre/+;GCaMP6f mice in the same manner. Identical puffs of 100 nM NKB directly above KNDy neurons were found to exert potent stimulatory effects on [Ca2+] in both males (N = 3) and females (N = 3) (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by GCaMP6 imaging data from 3 male and 3 female Kiss1Cre/+;GCaMP6f mice and referenced in Figures 4C and 4D.

claim: The effects of NKB on KNDy neuron [Ca2+] were more potent in males than in females (area under curve = 18,542 ± 2101 s. %F versus 5441 ± 1158, p<0.001).
source: The effects of NKB on KNDy neuron [Ca2+] were more potent in males than in females (area under curve = 18,542 ± 2101 s. %F versus 5441 ± 1158, p<0.001, Mann–Whitney test) (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by GCaMP6 imaging data with statistical analysis (Mann-Whitney test) and referenced in Figures 4C and 4D.

claim: Puffs of 200 nM dynorphin (90 s) had no significant effect on dendron [Ca2+] in either males or females.
source: Puffs of 200 nM dynorphin (90 s) were also found to have no significant effect on dendron [Ca2+] in either males (N = 11) or females (N = 11) (male, 2.83 ± 0.03%, median 2.86%; female, 2.14 ± 0.05%, median 2.19%) (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by GCaMP6 imaging data from 11 male and 11 female mice and referenced in Figures 5A and 5B.

claim: Dynorphin failed to alter dendron [Ca2+] on kisspeptin-evoked increases in males and females.
source: However, dynorphin continued to fail to alter dendron [Ca2+] in males (N = 5) and females (N = 4) (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by GCaMP6 imaging data from 5 male and 4 female mice and referenced in Figures 5C and 5D.

claim: A near-perfect fidelity between blue light activation and action currents was found for both 10 and 20 Hz stimulations in KNDy neurons.
source: A near-perfect fidelity between blue light activation and action currents was found for both 10 and 20 Hz stimulations (n = 8, in three mice; Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by optogenetic electrophysiology data from 8 cells in 3 mice and referenced in Figure 6A.

claim: 11 out of 40 unidentified ventrolateral ARN neurons responded to blue light activation of KNDy neurons.
source: Next, in these same mice, 40 unidentified ventrolateral ARN neurons surrounded by KNDy fibers were patched and the effects of 10 and 20 Hz stimulation examined. In total, 11 cells responded to blue light activation with nine exhibiting a slow-onset and prolonged (1–6 min, median 3 min) excitation (Figure 6B) and another two cells showing a similar temporal profile of suppressed firing (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by optogenetic electrophysiology data from 40 cells and referenced in Figures 6B and 6C.

claim: Nine unidentified ventrolateral ARN neurons exhibited slow-onset and prolonged (1–6 min, median 3 min) excitation in response to blue light activation of KNDy neurons.
source: In total, 11 cells responded to blue light activation with nine exhibiting a slow-onset and prolonged (1–6 min, median 3 min) excitation (Figure 6B) and another two cells showing a similar temporal profile of suppressed firing (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by optogenetic electrophysiology data and referenced in Figure 6B.

claim: Two unidentified ventrolateral ARN neurons showed suppressed firing in response to blue light activation of KNDy neurons.
source: In total, 11 cells responded to blue light activation with nine exhibiting a slow-onset and prolonged (1–6 min, median 3 min) excitation (Figure 6B) and another two cells showing a similar temporal profile of suppressed firing (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by optogenetic electrophysiology data and referenced in Figure 6C.

claim: ChR2-evoked increases in firing rate were reversibly inhibited by exposure to the NK3R antagonist SB222200 in five of nine cells.
source: The ChR2-evoked increases in firing rate were reversibly inhibited by exposure to the NK3R antagonist SB222200 in five of nine cells (Figure 6B) and inhibitions were reversibly blocked by the kappa-opioid antagonist nor-binaltorphimine (nor-BNI ) (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by optogenetic electrophysiology data with pharmacological manipulation and referenced in Figure 6B.

claim: Inhibitions of firing were reversibly blocked by the kappa-opioid antagonist nor-binaltorphimine (nor-BNI).
source: The ChR2-evoked increases in firing rate were reversibly inhibited by exposure to the NK3R antagonist SB222200 in five of nine cells (Figure 6B) and inhibitions were reversibly blocked by the kappa-opioid antagonist nor-binaltorphimine (nor-BNI ) (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by optogenetic electrophysiology data with pharmacological manipulation and referenced in Figure 6C.

claim: Kisspeptin has no effect on KNDy neuron excitability.
source: This is in striking contrast to signaling at the KNDy cell body where the opposite relationship exists with kisspeptin having no effect on excitability (de Croft et al., 2013), while the co-released neuropeptides NKB and dynorphin directly excite and inhibit firing, respectively (de Croft et al., 2013; Ruka et al., 2013; Qiu et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (de Croft et al., 2013).

claim: NKB and dynorphin directly excite and inhibit KNDy neuron firing, respectively.
source: This is in striking contrast to signaling at the KNDy cell body where the opposite relationship exists with kisspeptin having no effect on excitability (de Croft et al., 2013), while the co-released neuropeptides NKB and dynorphin directly excite and inhibit firing, respectively (de Croft et al., 2013; Ruka et al., 2013; Qiu et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (de Croft et al., 2013; Ruka et al., 2013; Qiu et al., 2016).

claim: Recurrent NKB and dynorphin signaling at the KNDy cell body underlies their synchronized episodic behavior.
source: It is proposed that the recurrent NKB and dynorphin signaling at the KNDy cell body underlies their synchronized episodic behavior (Qiu et al., 2016; Moore et al., 2018a).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Qiu et al., 2016; Moore et al., 2018a).

claim: Kiss1Cre/Cre mice in the homozygous state represent a Kiss-1 deletion.
source: In the homozygous state, the Kiss1Cre/Cre mice used in this study represent a Kiss-1 deletion (Yeo et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Yeo et al., 2016).

claim: Adult female null Kiss1Cre/Cre mice show complete absence of kisspeptin peptide in cells or fibers within the ARN while immunoreactivity for NKB remains.
source: To characterize these mice further, immunohistochemical analyses of adult female null Kiss1Cre/Cre mice (N = 4) confirmed the complete absence of kisspeptin peptide in cells or fibers within the ARN while immunoreactivity for NKB remained (Figure 7A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemical data from 4 female Kiss1Cre/Cre mice and referenced in Figures 7A-C.

claim: Both heterozygous Kiss1Cre/+ and homozygous Kiss1Cre/Cre KNDy neurons showed the same very low spontaneous firing rates (0.06 ± 0.04 Hz and 0.06 ± 0.06 Hz, respectively).
source: Both lines showed the same very low spontaneous firing rates (0.06 ± 0.04 Hz, n = 14, Kiss1Cre/+; 0.06 ± 0.06 Hz, n = 14, Kiss1Cre/Cre) typical of KNDy neurons (de Croft et al., 2012), and 50 nM NKB exerted the same marked stimulatory effect on firing (1.9 ± 0.4 Hz, n = 14, Kiss1Cre/+, 1.9 ± 0.6 Hz, n = 14, Kiss1Cre/Cre) (Figure 7D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiology data from 14 cells per genotype and referenced in Figures 7D and 7E.

claim: 50 nM NKB exerted the same marked stimulatory effect on firing in both heterozygous Kiss1Cre/+ (1.9 ± 0.4 Hz) and homozygous Kiss1Cre/Cre (1.9 ± 0.6 Hz) KNDy neurons.
source: Both lines showed the same very low spontaneous firing rates (0.06 ± 0.04 Hz, n = 14, Kiss1Cre/+; 0.06 ± 0.06 Hz, n = 14, Kiss1Cre/Cre) typical of KNDy neurons (de Croft et al., 2012), and 50 nM NKB exerted the same marked stimulatory effect on firing (1.9 ± 0.4 Hz, n = 14, Kiss1Cre/+, 1.9 ± 0.6 Hz, n = 14, Kiss1Cre/Cre) (Figure 7D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiology data from 14 cells per genotype and referenced in Figures 7D and 7E.

claim: The expression of NKB and function of NKB receptors in KNDy neurons is normal in the absence of kisspeptin in Kiss1-null mice.
source: Together, these studies indicate that the expression of NKB and function of NKB receptors in KNDy neurons is normal in the absence of kisspeptin in Kiss1-null mice.
evidence: The claim is inferred from immunohistochemical and electrophysiological data showing normal NKB expression and responses in Kiss1-null mice.

claim: 24 hour GCaMP fiber photometry recordings from adult female Kiss1Cre/Cre mice revealed the presence of frequent abrupt ARN kisspeptin neuron synchronizations.
source: Twenty-four hour GCaMP fiber photometry recordings from the middle/caudal ARN of adult female Kiss1Cre/Cre;Rosa26-tdT mice (N = 4) given prior injections of AAV9-CAG-FLEX-GCaMP6s, revealed the presence of frequent abrupt ARN kisspeptin neuron synchronizations (Figure 8A).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo GCaMP fiber photometry data from 4 female Kiss1Cre/Cre mice and referenced in Figure 8A.

claim: The pattern of KNDy neuron synchronization in Kiss1Cre/Cre mice is similar to that observed in ovariectomized heterozygous Kiss1Cre/+ mice.
source: This pattern is similar to that observed in ovariectomized heterozygous Kiss1Cre/+;Rosa26-tdT mice (Figure 8C) and compatible with homozygous Kiss1Cre/Cre mice being hypogonadal (Yeo et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of in vivo GCaMP fiber photometry data and referenced in Figure 8C.

claim: Homozygous Kiss1Cre/Cre mice are hypogonadal.
source: This pattern is similar to that observed in ovariectomized heterozygous Kiss1Cre/+;Rosa26-tdT mice (Figure 8C) and compatible with homozygous Kiss1Cre/Cre mice being hypogonadal (Yeo et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Yeo et al., 2016) and inference from the data.

claim: All four Kiss1-null mice exhibited an invariant, very low level of LH despite robust ARN KISS neuron synchronization events.
source: Despite robust ARNKISS neuron synchronization events (SEs), all four Kiss1-null mice exhibited an invariant, very low level of LH demonstrating a complete uncoupling of the KNDy pulse generator from LH secretion (Figure 8B).
evidence: The claim is supported by combined in vivo GCaMP fiber photometry and LH measurement data from 4 Kiss1-null mice and referenced in Figure 8B.

claim: Kiss1-null mice demonstrate a complete uncoupling of the KNDy pulse generator from LH secretion.
source: Despite robust ARNKISS neuron synchronization events (SEs), all four Kiss1-null mice exhibited an invariant, very low level of LH demonstrating a complete uncoupling of the KNDy pulse generator from LH secretion (Figure 8B).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that KNDy neuron synchronization events occur without corresponding LH pulses in Kiss1-null mice.

claim: All three ovariectomized Kiss1Cre/+ mice exhibited pulsatile LH secretion that was perfectly correlated with ARN kisspeptin neuron synchronization events.
source: In contrast, all three ovariectomized Kiss1Cre/+ mice exhibited pulsatile LH secretion that was perfectly correlated with ARN kisspeptin neuron SEs (Figure 8C).
evidence: The claim is supported by combined in vivo GCaMP fiber photometry and LH measurement data from 3 ovariectomized Kiss1Cre/+ mice and referenced in Figure 8C.

claim: Kisspeptin is the only co-transmitter active at the GnRH neuron dendron.
source: Kisspeptin is the only co-transmitter active at the GnRH neuron dendron, whereas the exact opposite situation exists at KNDy neuron recurrent collaterals where all of the co-transmitters, except kisspeptin, are active (Navarro et al., 2011; de Croft et al., 2013; Ruka et al., 2013; Qiu et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by GCaMP6 imaging data showing only kisspeptin activates GnRH dendrons.

claim: At KNDy neuron recurrent collaterals, all of the co-transmitters except kisspeptin are active.
source: Kisspeptin is the only co-transmitter active at the GnRH neuron dendron, whereas the exact opposite situation exists at KNDy neuron recurrent collaterals where all of the co-transmitters, except kisspeptin, are active (Navarro et al., 2011; de Croft et al., 2013; Ruka et al., 2013; Qiu et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Navarro et al., 2011; de Croft et al., 2013; Ruka et al., 2013; Qiu et al., 2016).

claim: Deletion of kisspeptin from KNDy neurons abolishes episodic hormone secretion while maintaining KNDy neuron synchronization behavior.
source: We demonstrate that this mode of co-transmission is physiologically relevant in vivo as deletion of kisspeptin from the repertoire of transmitters used by KNDy neurons abolishes episodic hormone secretion while maintaining KNDy neuron synchronization behavior.
evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo GCaMP fiber photometry and LH measurement data from Kiss1-null mice.

claim: GnRH neuron cell bodies are scattered throughout the basal forebrain as a result of their migration from the nose into the brain at mid-gestation.
source: As a result of their migration from the nose into the brain at mid-gestation, the GnRH neuron cell bodies are scattered throughout the basal forebrain (Wray, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Wray, 2010).

claim: GnRH neurons focus their blended dendritic/axonal projections on the ME where they can be regulated in a concerted manner by the KNDy pulse generator.
source: The functional difficulties imposed by this topography appear to be solved, in part, by GnRH neurons focusing their blended dendritic/axonal projections on the ME where they can be regulated in a concerted manner by the KNDy pulse generator (Herbison, 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Herbison, 2018) and inference from anatomical data.

claim: Classic synaptic inputs exist on the GnRH neuron dendron.
source: While it is clear that classic synaptic inputs exist on the GnRH neuron dendron (Moore et al., 2018b; Wang et al., 2020), we note that this is not the case for the KNDy neuron innervation.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Moore et al., 2018b; Wang et al., 2020).

claim: An electron microscopic investigation in the rat reported that closely apposed kisspeptin fibers and GnRH neuron nerve terminals in the ME do not form synapses.
source: An electron microscopic investigation in the rat also reported that closely apposed kisspeptin fibers and GnRH neuron nerve terminals in the ME do not form synapses (Uenoyama et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior electron microscopy literature (Uenoyama et al., 2011).

claim: The morphological relationship between KNDy fibers and GnRH neuron dendrons is indicative of short-distance volume transmission.
source: This morphological relationship is indicative of short-distance volume transmission (van den Pol, 2012).
evidence: The claim is inferred from expansion microscopy data showing non-synaptic appositions and supported by citation (van den Pol, 2012).

claim: Individual KNDy fibers form appositions with multiple GnRH neuron dendrons.
source: We also note that individual KNDy fibers form appositions with multiple GnRH neuron dendrons.
evidence: The claim is supported by anatomical data.

claim: The synchronous activation of GnRH neuron dendrons is achieved by volume transmission originating from multiple boutons of KNDy neuron axons winding their way through GnRH neuron dendrons.
source: Thus, it seems probable that the synchronous activation of GnRH neuron dendrons is achieved by volume transmission originating from multiple boutons of KNDy neuron axons winding their way through GnRH neuron dendrons.
evidence: The claim is inferred from anatomical and functional data showing non-synaptic appositions and divergent innervation.

claim: KNDy neurons only project to the GnRH neuron distal projections in and around the ME in the mouse.
source: Studies in the mouse show that KNDy neurons only project to the GnRH neuron distal projections in an around the ME (Yip et al., 2015; Qiu et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Yip et al., 2015; Qiu et al., 2016).

claim: Immunohistochemical studies have indicated that GnRH neurons express receptors for NKB and/or dynorphin.
source: Although immunohistochemical studies have indicated that GnRH neurons express receptors for NKB and/or dynorphin (Krajewski et al., 2005; Weems et al., 2016), this has not been supported by mRNA profiling and electrophysiological studies (Mitchell et al., 1997; Sannella and Petersen, 1997; Navarro et al., 2011; Qiu et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior immunohistochemical literature (Krajewski et al., 2005; Weems et al., 2016).

claim: mRNA profiling and electrophysiological studies have not supported the expression of NKB and/or dynorphin receptors on GnRH neurons.
source: Although immunohistochemical studies have indicated that GnRH neurons express receptors for NKB and/or dynorphin (Krajewski et al., 2005; Weems et al., 2016), this has not been supported by mRNA profiling and electrophysiological studies (Mitchell et al., 1997; Sannella and Petersen, 1997; Navarro et al., 2011; Qiu et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior mRNA profiling and electrophysiological literature (Mitchell et al., 1997; Sannella and Petersen, 1997; Navarro et al., 2011; Qiu et al., 2016).

claim: GnRH neuron dendrons are not likely to express NK3R.
source: We find here that NKB had no effects on [Ca2+] in GnRH neuron dendrons, indicating that they are not likely to express NK3R.
evidence: The claim is inferred from GCaMP6 imaging data showing no response to NKB.

claim: Dynorphin signaling is not involved in terminating the kisspeptin-evoked GnRH pulse at the level of the GnRH neuron, at least in mice.
source: The latter result does not support the hypothesis that dynorphin signaling is involved in terminating the kisspeptin-evoked GnRH pulse at the level of the GnRH neuron, at least in mice (Weems et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is inferred from GCaMP6 imaging data showing no effect of dynorphin on kisspeptin-evoked responses and contrasted with a prior hypothesis (Weems et al., 2018).

claim: Nitric oxide can terminate and re-set kisspeptin responses at the GnRH neuron cell body.
source: Notably, a very recent study has shown that nitric oxide can terminate and re-set kisspeptin responses at the GnRH neuron cell body (Constantin et al., 2021), and it is possible that a similar scenario exists at the level of the GnRH neuron dendron.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a recent study (Constantin et al., 2021).

claim: It is possible that nitric oxide terminates and re-sets kisspeptin responses at the level of the GnRH neuron dendron.
source: Notably, a very recent study has shown that nitric oxide can terminate and re-set kisspeptin responses at the GnRH neuron cell body (Constantin et al., 2021), and it is possible that a similar scenario exists at the level of the GnRH neuron dendron.
evidence: The claim is speculative, extrapolating from findings at the cell body to the dendron.

claim: There is a falling gradient of glutamate receptor expression along the GnRH neuron projections.
source: Hence, it seems very likely that there is falling gradient of glutamate receptor expression along the GnRH neuron projections such that, while glutamate will activate those rare dendrons coming from GnRH neuron somata close by the ME, 99% of distal dendrons have no glutamate receptors.
evidence: The claim is inferred from current and prior GCaMP6 imaging data showing differential glutamate responses along the projection.

claim: Low-frequency KNDy neuron activation, which would be presumed to release only glutamate, has no impact on LH secretion.
source: Functionally, it is notable that low-frequency KNDy neuron activation, that would be presumed to release only glutamate, has no impact on LH secretion (Han et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Han et al., 2015).

claim: KNDy neurons package their individual neurotransmitters into separate vesicles.
source: As KNDy neurons package their individual neurotransmitters into separate vesicles (Murakawa et al., 2016), they could differentially traffic specific vesicles to distinct axonal projections.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Murakawa et al., 2016).

claim: KNDy neuron recurrent collaterals and their projections to GnRH neuron dendrons all co-express kisspeptin, NKB, and dynorphin.
source: However, this does not appear to occur at their two key efferent outputs for regulating pulsatile LH secretion as KNDy neuron recurrent collaterals and their projections to GnRH neuron dendrons all co-express kisspeptin, NKB, and dynorphin (Lehman et al., 2010; Figure 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Lehman et al., 2010) and data from Figure 1.

claim: Kisspeptin, NKB, and dynorphin are all released from KNDy terminals adjacent to the GnRH neuron dendron.
source: In agreement, we find evidence that kisspeptin, NKB, and dynorphin are all released from KNDy terminals adjacent to the GnRH neuron dendron, while Qui and colleagues demonstrated that NKB and dynorphin were released at recurrent collaterals innervating the KNDy cell bodies (Qiu et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by optogenetic electrophysiology data showing responses to released neuropeptides.

claim: NKB and dynorphin are released at recurrent collaterals innervating the KNDy cell bodies.
source: In agreement, we find evidence that kisspeptin, NKB, and dynorphin are all released from KNDy terminals adjacent to the GnRH neuron dendron, while Qui and colleagues demonstrated that NKB and dynorphin were released at recurrent collaterals innervating the KNDy cell bodies (Qiu et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Qiu et al., 2016).

claim: A population of unidentified neurons located in the ventrolateral ARN may have their activity entrained by the GnRH neuron pulse generator.
source: These observations also suggest that a population of unidentified neurons located in the ventrolateral ARN may have their activity entrained by the GnRH neuron pulse generator.
evidence: The claim is inferred from optogenetic electrophysiology data showing responses of unidentified neurons to KNDy neuron activation.

claim: There is evidence for both NKB- and dynorphin-receptive neurons in the ventrolateral ARN responding to KNDy neuron activation.
source: We found evidence for both NKB- and dynorphin-receptive neurons in this area responding to KNDy neuron activation as well as cells excited in a NK3R-independent manner that may be activated by kisspeptin (Fu and van den Pol, 2010; Liu and Herbison, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by optogenetic electrophysiology data with pharmacological manipulation and citations to prior literature (Fu and van den Pol, 2010; Liu and Herbison, 2015).

claim: Cells in the ventrolateral ARN excited in a NK3R-independent manner may be activated by kisspeptin.
source: We found evidence for both NKB- and dynorphin-receptive neurons in this area responding to KNDy neuron activation as well as cells excited in a NK3R-independent manner that may be activated by kisspeptin (Fu and van den Pol, 2010; Liu and Herbison, 2015).
evidence: The claim is speculative, inferred from optogenetic data and supported by citations (Fu and van den Pol, 2010; Liu and Herbison, 2015).

claim: The GnRH pulse generator network uses converse patterns of post-synaptic receptor expression at the two main targets of the KNDy neuron required for episodic hormone secretion.
source: In summary, evidence indicates that the GnRH pulse generator network uses converse patterns of post-synaptic receptor expression at the two main targets of the KNDy neuron required for episodic hormone secretion.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined anatomical, functional, and in vivo data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Converse patterns of post-synaptic receptor expression solve the problem of signal resolution generated when using neuropeptide volume transmission in the close vicinity of the KNDy somata and GnRH neuron dendrons.
source: This likely solves the problem of signal resolution generated when using neuropeptide volume transmission in the close vicinity of the KNDy somata and GnRH neuron dendrons.
evidence: The claim is speculative, proposing a functional explanation for the observed receptor expression patterns.

claim: This pattern of co-transmission enables neurons to achieve differential signaling at varied targets without the need for selective trafficking of neuropeptide transmitters throughout their axonal arbor.
source: Although highly redundant at the level of the post-synaptic space, this novel pattern of co-transmission enables neurons to achieve differential signaling at varied targets without the need for selective trafficking of neuropeptide transmitters throughout their axonal arbor.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined data showing uniform transmitter expression but differential receptor expression.

claim: ~69% of KNDy neurons express GCaMP6 with the AAV approach used.
source: In brief, ~69% of KNDy neurons express GCaMP6 with this AAV approach and 96% of all GCaMP-expressing cells in the ARN are kisspeptin neurons.
evidence: The claim is supported by characterization of the AAV transduction method.

claim: 96% of all GCaMP-expressing cells in the ARN are kisspeptin neurons.
source: In brief, ~69% of KNDy neurons express GCaMP6 with this AAV approach and 96% of all GCaMP-expressing cells in the ARN are kisspeptin neurons.
evidence: The claim is supported by characterization of the AAV transduction method.

claim: Using expansion microscopy, KNDy neurons make abundant close, non-synaptic appositions with the GnRH neuron dendron.
source: Using expansion microscopy, we show that KNDy neurons make abundant close, non-synaptic appositions with the GnRH neuron dendron.
evidence: The claim is supported by expansion microscopy data.

claim: Despite all three neuropeptides being released from KNDy terminals, only kisspeptin was able to activate the GnRH neuron dendron.
source: Electrophysiology and confocal GCaMP6 imaging demonstrated that, despite all three neuropeptides being released from KNDy terminals, only kisspeptin was able to activate the GnRH neuron dendron.
evidence: The claim is supported by GCaMP6 imaging and optogenetic electrophysiology data.

claim: Mice with a selective deletion of kisspeptin from KNDy neurons failed to exhibit pulsatile hormone secretion.
source: Mice with a selective deletion of kisspeptin from KNDy neurons failed to exhibit pulsatile hormone secretion but maintained synchronized episodic KNDy neuron behavior that is thought to depend on recurrent NKB and dynorphin transmission.
evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo GCaMP fiber photometry and LH measurement data from Kiss1-null mice.

claim: Mice with a selective deletion of kisspeptin from KNDy neurons maintained synchronized episodic KNDy neuron behavior.
source: Mice with a selective deletion of kisspeptin from KNDy neurons failed to exhibit pulsatile hormone secretion but maintained synchronized episodic KNDy neuron behavior that is thought to depend on recurrent NKB and dynorphin transmission.
evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo GCaMP fiber photometry data from Kiss1-null mice.

claim: Synchronized episodic KNDy neuron behavior is thought to depend on recurrent NKB and dynorphin transmission.
source: Mice with a selective deletion of kisspeptin from KNDy neurons failed to exhibit pulsatile hormone secretion but maintained synchronized episodic KNDy neuron behavior that is thought to depend on recurrent NKB and dynorphin transmission.
evidence: The claim is supported by inference from the Kiss1-null mouse data and established knowledge about KNDy neuron signaling.

claim: KNDy neurons drive episodic hormone secretion through highly redundant neuropeptide co-transmission orchestrated by differential post-synaptic neuropeptide receptor expression at the GnRH neuron dendron and KNDy neuron.
source: This indicates that KNDy neurons drive episodic hormone secretion through highly redundant neuropeptide co-transmission orchestrated by differential post-synaptic neuropeptide receptor expression at the GnRH neuron dendron and KNDy neuron.
evidence: The claim is the main conclusion inferred from all the experimental data presented in the manuscript.
